semantics.note: The normalization preserves the numerical range and comparison classes.

contract.note: Electrical capacity is an ordinary reading given the surrounding megawatt comparisons. Requiring representative data and consistent facility boundaries fairly tests the general assertion.

evidence.note: Authentic earlier illustrative capacities imply a fourfold ratio, but do not establish a representative August 2026 comparison between the specified workloads.
IREN discloses a 50 MW GPU site at December 2025. This company disclosure lacks a matched comparator and evidence establishing the publication-date inventory.

reviews.rationale: Neither item supplies representative, contemporaneous comparisons with consistent power definitions, facility boundaries and project status. The smaller historical examples do not establish or refute the general 10-to-100-fold range.

attribution.note: The guarantee and its business-model explanation are Zitron's own assertions.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves a firm prediction and its asserted economic explanation. Its general pricing language must retain the source's broad scope.

contract.note: Price or paid-plan terms is a reasonable reading. However, changes at three selected vendors cannot settle the guarantee covering whatever users currently pay. Stability over an unspecified long period also cannot contradict a forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: Stable subscription medians over one month do not contradict an indefinite forecast. Model and plan replacements change the basket, but do not establish broad repricing caused by unsettled business models.
The announcement was available before the cutoff, but its API price change takes effect afterward. It does not establish a completed outcome or the required broad economic explanation.
Ending new subscriptions establishes an availability change for prospective customers, not changed payments or terms for existing subscribers. No economic cause is established.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was supplied. The packet neither establishes the broad guaranteed change and its economic cause nor meets even the contract's narrower three-vendor trigger. Short-term stability cannot establish failure.

attribution.note: Zitron directly makes the guarantee about paying users.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves paying-user scope, the guarantee, the disjunction, the indefinite horizon and the economic link.

contract.note: One qualifying event can satisfy the disjunction for affected users, but cannot establish a guarantee for paying users across LLM services. The early-resolution rule improperly substitutes one provider for that broader scope; finite stability likewise cannot refute an indefinite forecast.

evidence.note: Reports an announced post-publication weekly-limit reduction across Claude paid plans. It supports the forecast for affected Claude users, but predates implementation and cannot establish the universal guarantee.
Corroborates the announced change and paid-plan coverage. Moving from 150 to 125 baseline units is a roughly 17% reduction; the report precedes its effective date.
The reporter describes rising costs alongside limit management. This supplies economic background, but does not independently establish that costs caused this particular reduction.
The temporary promotion and retained session-limit improvements qualify the severity of the change. They do not negate a weekly-rate-limit shift.

reviews.rationale: The reports support an announced rate-limit shift for Claude subscribers, with economic background. They do not establish the guarantee across paying users of LLM services. The contract's single-provider trigger cannot fairly close that broader forecast, which has no deadline.

attribution.note: Zitron endorses the financial assertions in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization fairly extracts the factual expenditure and revenue assertions while excluding the evaluative description.

contract.note: Realized revenue over the latest completed fiscal year is an ordinary reading of annual revenue. Requiring an identified capex period and AI allocation avoids inventing expenditure scope.

evidence.note: Microsoft's company disclosure reports total AI annualized revenue, including OpenAI. It cannot establish realized annual revenue excluding OpenAI.
Microsoft discloses one quarter of company-wide capex, including finance leases and infrastructure for both AI and non-AI workloads. This does not establish cumulative AI-attributable expenditure.

reviews.rationale: The packet supplies neither realized annual AI revenue excluding OpenAI nor a reconciliation of cumulative AI-specific capex. Total AI run rate and quarterly company-wide expenditure cannot settle either threshold on the required basis.
